## Themes

These rows serve two capabilities. Vetting a measured number before it is reported, compared or acted on: principle-explain-the-number keeps what makes a number evidence, and performance-optimization takes the procedure. Keeping a reviewable record of a long run's decisions: a decision-trail skill owns the append-only log, its end-of-run audit and its independent review.

### Blind extraction

1. answers-from-run-evidence: Every checklist question must be settled with data from an actual run, and reasoning about the code does not count. (SKILL.md:9)
2. single-run-ballpark-allowance: When the user asked only for a rough figure, a single run is sufficient. (SKILL.md:11)
3. ballpark-keeps-error-and-work-checks: Even a rough single-run figure must still pass the error check and the did-the-work-run check. (SKILL.md:11)
4. ballpark-discloses-run-count: A rough figure must state that it rests on one run. (SKILL.md:11)
5. ballpark-escalates-when-suspicious: On the rough path the remaining questions may be dropped unless the run's result looks off, in which case they apply. (SKILL.md:11)
6. option-choice-excluded-from-ballpark: A measurement used to choose between options can never take the rough path. (SKILL.md:11)
7. claim-written-before-measuring: Before any run, write out the exact result sentence you expect to publish, including metric and dataset. (SKILL.md:15)
8. questions-test-the-claim-sentence: The checklist questions are applied against that pre-written sentence rather than against the raw numbers. (SKILL.md:15)
9. read-measurement-script-first: Read the measuring script beforehand and record what it times, what it counts and what it leaves out. (SKILL.md:16)
10. machine-load-precheck: Check the load average and the core count before measuring. (SKILL.md:17)
11. identify-competing-load: If the machine is busy, find out which work is occupying it. (SKILL.md:17)
12. interleave-under-unavoidable-noise: If the competing work cannot be stopped, interleave the compared sides so both experience the same interference. (SKILL.md:17)
13. disclose-noise-interleaving: State in the report that interleaving was used because of unstoppable background load. (SKILL.md:17)
14. name-the-limiter: Identify the specific resource or code path that stops the result from being twice as good. (SKILL.md:21)
15. profile-in-unreported-run: Do profiling and tracing in a separate run whose numbers are never reported, because instrumentation distorts timing. (SKILL.md:21)
16. per-process-cpu-signal: Inspect CPU use per process when hunting the limiter. (SKILL.md:21)
17. runtime-profiler-signal: Use a language or system profiler when hunting the limiter. (SKILL.md:21)
18. io-wait-signal: Inspect I/O wait when hunting the limiter. (SKILL.md:21)
19. syscall-count-signal: Inspect system call counts when hunting the limiter. (SKILL.md:21)
20. map-hotspot-to-source: Trace the observed hot spot back to the source code responsible. (SKILL.md:21)
21. load-generator-saturation-check: Monitor the load generator as well, since a saturated generator means the measurement describes the generator and not the target. (SKILL.md:21)
22. limiter-before-dismissing-change: When a change leaves the number unmoved, find the limiter before concluding the change has no value. (SKILL.md:21)
23. production-build-and-flags-parity: Run every side with production builds, flags and environment. (SKILL.md:22)
24. production-batching-and-transaction-parity: Run every side with production batching and transaction settings. (SKILL.md:22)
25. production-connection-pool-parity: Run every side with production connection pool settings. (SKILL.md:22)
26. production-cache-temperature-parity: Run every side with caches as warm or as cold as production has them. (SKILL.md:22)
27. same-versions-and-data-parity: Run every side on identical versions and identical data. (SKILL.md:22)
28. default-config-invalidates-comparison: If one side runs on defaults, treat the result as a comparison of configurations rather than of implementations. (SKILL.md:22)
29. settings-limiter-means-untuned: A limiter that turns out to be a setting, such as per-row commits, a debug build or an absent index, classifies that side as untuned. (SKILL.md:22)
30. tune-and-remeasure-before-winner: An untuned side must be tuned and measured again before a winner is named. (SKILL.md:22)
31. no-winner-if-untunable: If tuning a side is not possible, that run may not produce a winner. (SKILL.md:22)
32. no-claim-narrowing-for-adoption: When the user is deciding what to adopt, restricting the claim to the current as-shipped settings does not cure an untuned comparison. (SKILL.md:22)
33. bandwidth-sanity-arithmetic: Compare computed bytes per second against disk and network capacity. (SKILL.md:23)
34. core-budget-sanity-arithmetic: Multiply operations per second by cost per operation and compare the product against available cores. (SKILL.md:23)
35. removed-share-gain-bound: Check the claimed saving against the time the changed part took, since removing a fraction of a run caps the speedup accordingly. (SKILL.md:23)
36. past-limit-means-wrong-target: A result beyond a computed limit is read as having measured something else, such as a cache, a no-op or a defect. (SKILL.md:23)
37. count-failures-and-non-success: Tally failures and non-success responses, because fast rejections and slow timeouts both skew timing. (SKILL.md:24)
38. verify-output-correctness: Check that outputs are correct and not merely present. (SKILL.md:24)
39. add-missing-error-count: If the measuring script has no error count, add one. (SKILL.md:24)
40. minimum-five-runs-per-side: Run each compared side at least five times. (SKILL.md:25)
41. alternate-side-order: Alternate the sides run by run so warmup, lazy initialization, caches and drift favor neither. (SKILL.md:25)
42. report-median-and-range: Report the median and the range across runs. (SKILL.md:25)
43. gap-under-variation-is-no-difference: A gap smaller than run-to-run variation is reported as no measurable difference. (SKILL.md:25)
44. statistical-test-when-close: When the outcome is close, use a rank-sum test or the statistics built into the measuring harness. (SKILL.md:25)
45. end-to-end-beside-micro: Whenever a micro result is produced, also measure the whole path a user waits on. (SKILL.md:26)
46. realistic-size-and-concurrency: The end-to-end measurement uses realistic data sizes and concurrency. (SKILL.md:26)
47. report-micro-as-share: Express the micro result as a proportion of the whole path. (SKILL.md:26)
48. share-caps-user-visible-gain: A component's share of a request is treated as the ceiling on how much the request can improve. (SKILL.md:26)
49. confirm-work-inside-timed-region: Confirm the work executed within the timed span, for example that the server got the request, rows were persisted and bytes were read. (SKILL.md:27)
50. confirm-result-consumed: Confirm the code actually used the result, guarding against unconsumed generators, unawaited promises and results a JIT can drop. (SKILL.md:27)
51. timeout-phantom-number-guard: Treat a number produced by a timeout as possibly describing work that never ran. (SKILL.md:27)
52. verdict-first: The report opens with the verdict. (SKILL.md:31)
53. four-value-verdict-vocabulary: The verdict is one of faster, slower, no measurable difference or inconclusive. (SKILL.md:31)
54. number-carries-unit-runs-range-limiter: A reported figure comes with its unit, run count, range and limiter. (SKILL.md:32)
55. inconclusive-without-limiter: A claimed difference whose limiter cannot be named must be called inconclusive. (SKILL.md:33)
56. inconclusive-when-side-untuned: A verdict must be inconclusive when any side ran untuned. (SKILL.md:33)
57. inconclusive-without-error-or-work-check: A verdict must be inconclusive when the error check or the did-the-work-run check could not be done. (SKILL.md:33)
58. name-the-gap: An inconclusive verdict states which check or condition caused it. (SKILL.md:33)
59. one-primary-number-in-pr-body: A pull request description carries a single primary number. (SKILL.md:34)
60. supporting-evidence-outside-pr-body: Runs, range and limiter evidence go in a linked artifact or notes file rather than the pull request description. (SKILL.md:34)
61. vet-baseline-before-planning: In a performance-issue flow, the baseline is put through the checklist before any plan is built from it. (SKILL.md:38)
62. vet-every-later-number: In a performance-issue flow, each number after the baseline is also put through the checklist. (SKILL.md:38)
63. vet-harness-before-freeze: In an iterative optimization loop, the harness is put through the checklist before it is frozen. (SKILL.md:39)
64. frozen-harness-prints-error-and-work-counts: In an iterative optimization loop, the frozen harness emits error and work counts so each keep-or-revert decision gets those two checks automatically. (SKILL.md:39)

Purpose: Upstream keeps a reviewable decision log for a long run, audited and independently reviewed. Ours has no unit for this until decision-trail is built.
Reason: Compared with none: decision-trail, the row target, does not exist yet, and --with takes only an existing skill. Suggested beads by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. single-canonical-log: Work keeps exactly one authoritative decision log. (SKILL.md:9)
2. tsv-one-row-per-decision: The log is one tab-separated file where each decision takes one row. (SKILL.md:13)
3. single-line-cells: No cell may span more than one line. (SKILL.md:13)
4. evidence-as-pointer: The evidence cell holds a resolvable reference such as a commit, PR number, file and line, or artifact, trace or screenshot path, and never narrative. (SKILL.md:13, SKILL.md:21)
5. header-template-seed: A new log starts from a supplied file holding only the header row. (SKILL.md:15, references/decision-log-template.tsv:1)
6. six-column-schema: Rows have the fixed columns timestamp, phase, decision, why, evidence and result. (SKILL.md:17-22, references/decision-log-template.tsv:1)
7. iso8601-timestamp-column: The timestamp column uses ISO8601. (SKILL.md:17)
8. phase-or-workstream-column: A column attributes each row to its phase or workstream. (SKILL.md:18)
9. one-line-decision-column: The decision column says in one line what was chosen or done. (SKILL.md:19)
10. plain-reason-column: The why column gives the reason plainly, and a guiding principle is spelled out instead of cited as a jargon tag. (SKILL.md:20)
11. result-as-outcome-or-predicate-state: The result column records an outcome or a state such as passing tests, reverted, zero visual diff, inconclusive or open. (SKILL.md:22)
12. worked-example-rows: A sample log shows the expected plain style, including a row for discarding a helper's output after checking the real files. (SKILL.md:26-32)
13. teammate-voice-log-text: Rows are written as you would describe the action to a colleague, in concrete terms and free of machine-sounding or abstract language. (SKILL.md:36)
14. helper-script-for-rows: A script takes the log path and five cell values and appends a well-formed row. (SKILL.md:38, scripts/log.sh:1-3)
15. manual-append-sanitization-caveat: Appending by hand is allowed, but cells from generated or user-supplied text need the same byte-level care the script applies. (SKILL.md:38)
16. log-decision-points-not-actions: Rows are for decision points and checkpoints, not for each action taken. (SKILL.md:40)
17. checkpoint-row-categories: Row-worthy events are a chosen fork, a finished unit with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its cause, a surfaced blocker and a fixed gate. (SKILL.md:40)
18. one-row-per-loop-iteration: Looping runs write one row for each iteration. (SKILL.md:40)
19. skip-trivial-rows: Trivial or self-evident steps get no row. (SKILL.md:40)
20. strict-shell-failure-mode: The script aborts on any command failure, unset variable or pipeline failure. (scripts/log.sh:4)
21. argument-count-guard: The script prints usage and exits non-zero unless given exactly six arguments. (scripts/log.sh:6-9)
22. auto-create-log-directory: The script creates the log's parent directory when it is missing. (scripts/log.sh:14-17)
23. header-on-empty-log: The script writes the header row when the log is missing or empty. (scripts/log.sh:21-23)
24. header-write-never-truncates: The header is written in append mode, so a false empty-file test on a network mount costs a stray header and no rows. (scripts/log.sh:19-22)
25. automatic-utc-timestamp: The script stamps each row with the current UTC time so the caller does not supply it. (scripts/log.sh:25)
26. strip-cell-control-whitespace: The script replaces tabs, newlines and carriage returns in each cell with spaces. (scripts/log.sh:26, scripts/log.sh:34)
27. spreadsheet-formula-neutralization: The script prefixes a single quote to any cell starting with a formula-triggering character, so hostile evidence text cannot execute when opened in a spreadsheet. (SKILL.md:38, scripts/log.sh:26-38)
28. append-only-row-write: The script adds the row with an append redirect. (scripts/log.sh:40-42)
29. run-boundary-definition: A run is one agent conversation with its later turns and summaries, while a pickup, replacement agent or new chat counts as a new run. (SKILL.md:42)
30. start-row-on-existing-log: A run adding to a log that already has rows first writes a row with the phase `start`. (SKILL.md:42)
31. start-row-after-foreign-start: A run writes a fresh `start` row when its next row follows another run's `start` row. (SKILL.md:42)
32. reread-log-tail-on-return: A run returning to a log in a later turn first reads the last rows to detect writes by other runs. (SKILL.md:42)
33. start-row-names-foreign-range: A `start` row records the timestamp range of the preceding rows that this run did not write. (SKILL.md:42)
34. start-row-evidence-identifies-run: The evidence cell of a `start` row identifies the current run, for example by agent id. (SKILL.md:42)
35. reserved-start-phase: The phase value `start` is used for no other purpose. (SKILL.md:42)
36. uncommitted-working-artifact-default: By default the log is a working file kept out of version control. (SKILL.md:46)
37. default-log-path: The default location is a fixed-name TSV in the work directory. (SKILL.md:46)
38. per-task-path-when-concurrent: When several efforts run at once, each log goes in a hidden audit directory under a task-slug filename. (SKILL.md:46)
39. commit-only-for-reviewer-trust: The log is committed only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the outcome. (SKILL.md:48)
40. append-only-history: Rows are never edited or deleted, and a wrong call is corrected by a later row that supersedes it. (SKILL.md:52)
41. prefer-committed-script-evidence: Evidence generated by committed scripts is favored over hand-made one-off evidence. (SKILL.md:53)
42. end-of-run-log-audit: Before handing back, the run checks its log for truthfulness against what happened. (SKILL.md:57)
43. audit-reads-own-transcript: The audit uses this run's transcript from the active workspace's transcript directory, whose location comes from the system prompt. (SKILL.md:57)
44. no-cross-project-transcript-glob: The audit must not search across all project transcript folders, because that exposes unrelated private conversations. (SKILL.md:57)
45. audit-scoped-to-own-stretches: The audit covers only the row stretches belonging to this run, delimited by its `start` rows or the log's first row and the next `start` row of another run. (SKILL.md:57, SKILL.md:63)
46. row-maps-to-real-event: Each audited row must correspond to a decision or action that actually occurred. (SKILL.md:59)
47. evidence-resolves-and-supports: Each audited row's evidence must resolve and must show what the row asserts. (SKILL.md:60)
48. unlogged-fork-is-gap: A fork, pivot or abandoned path that shaped the work without a row is a gap that the audit adds. (SKILL.md:61)
49. audit-corrects-by-superseding: The audit changes nothing in place, even for an invented row, and instead adds a superseding row stating what really happened with a resolving pointer. (SKILL.md:63)
50. supersede-foreign-row-on-evidence: A row outside the audited stretches is superseded only when this run's own work shows it to be wrong. (SKILL.md:63)
51. different-model-family-reviewer: Before handing back, a subagent from a different model family reviews the run, and the author's self-review does not replace it. (SKILL.md:67)
52. reviewer-reads-trail-and-transcript: The reviewer's inputs are the audit trail and the run's transcript. (SKILL.md:67)
53. attention-scan-not-redo: The reviewer looks for what is suboptimal or risky for the user's attention and does not repeat the work. (SKILL.md:67)
54. reviewer-effort-and-speed-choice: Each reviewer's reasoning level and speed tier are chosen to suit the job. (SKILL.md:67)
55. flag-weak-evidence: The reviewer flags logged decisions with thin or missing evidence. (SKILL.md:69)
56. flag-unproven-verification: The reviewer flags verification that was skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript. (SKILL.md:70)
57. flag-hindsight-risky-choices: The reviewer flags choices that look premature, scope-expanding or symptom-masking in hindsight. (SKILL.md:71)
58. flag-skim-invisible-gaps: The reviewer flags gaps a user would miss on a casual read. (SKILL.md:72)
59. attention-section-closes-reply: Every reply for a run that produced a trail ends with a section called Attention. (SKILL.md:74)
60. reviewer-model-name-line: The Attention section opens with a line of its own naming the reviewer's model. (SKILL.md:74)
61. flags-point-to-rows-or-moments: Each listed flag cites specific rows or moments. (SKILL.md:74)
62. no-flags-allowed-model-name-required: An empty flag list is acceptable, but the reviewer's model name may not be omitted. (SKILL.md:74)
63. reader-walkthrough-method: A human reviewer reads from top to bottom, follows the evidence pointers and spot-checks. (SKILL.md:78)
64. github-table-rendering: Committing the TSV gives reviewers a table view on GitHub. (SKILL.md:78)
65. terminal-column-rendering: The `column` command with a tab separator displays the log as a table in a terminal. (SKILL.md:78)
66. single-owner-of-trail-format: Other skills needing an audit trail refer to this one by name and do not define their own trail or repeat its columns. (SKILL.md:82)
